episodes.title: I Exposed the Most Evil Cult in Mexico...
episodes.description:
This documentary presents opposing perspectives. Current members of La Luz del Mundo regard Naasón Joaquín García as the Apostle of Jesus Christ, maintain his innocence, and view the prosecutions as religious persecution. Former members describe a system of coercive control and abuse, and dozens of survivors cooperated with investigators. These views cannot both be true, so here is the legal record: In 2022, Joaquín García pleaded guilty in California to sexually abusing minor followers and was sentenced to 16 years and 8 months in prison, where he remains today. In 2025, he was further indicted on federal racketeering and sex trafficking charges, for which he is presumed innocent unless convicted; that case is ongoing. We encourage viewers to weigh the accounts in this film against that record.

Content note: This documentary discusses sexual abuse, including abuse of minors. Descriptions of that abuse are included only to the extent necessary to establish the nature, scale, and severity of the conduct committed and concealed by the church's senior leadership: as documented in court records and survivor testimony. Nothing in this film is presented for shock value, and graphic detail has been deliberately withheld. This is an examination of the leadership of an institution, not of its members or their faith.

This documentary is produced for educational and journalistic purposes. It does not target any faith, but it does examine coercive control. If you or someone you love is in a high-control group: manipulation, isolation from family, punishment for questioning, and fear of leaving are not normal features of a healthy community. Help and information: ICSA (International Cultic Studies Association) – icsahome.com | Cult Education Institute – culteducation.com | If you're in immediate danger, call 911.

This is a documentary investigation into the leadership of La Luz del Mundo, produced in the public interest. Its purpose is to educate viewers about how institutional abuse and coercive control operate — using court records, adjudicated convictions, and firsthand accounts. This film condemns the abuse it documents. Where abuse is described, it is only to the extent necessary to establish what the church's senior leadership did and concealed. Nothing here is shown for shock value, graphic detail has been withheld, and viewer discretion is advised. This is an examination of an institution's leaders — not its members, and not their faith. Resources for anyone affected are in the description.
